notes:
Passed the fake backend only; evidence_state is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level and never a hardware run. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null). It binds one of the card's four entry classes, DAQ_2DViewer_ThorlabsPLL, the Thorlabs 2D viewer; the Basler, Andor and PCO viewers name other pylablib camera families and are not covered, because a Driver has one native class. Reads: the serial numbers the Thorlabs enumeration reports at import, the camera information string, the exposure in seconds, the detector size and the six values of the pylablib ROI (hstart, hend, vstart, vend, hbin, vbin). Writes: exposure and the six ROI/binning values through the viewer's update_rois. All seven writes are Limit.operator_required: no text of the clone states the usable range of an installed camera (the viewer's 1 ms and limits [1, 2] are UI defaults, daq_2Dviewer_GenericPylablibCamera.py:26-30), so site-limits.example.json is only an example overlay, not a statement about any camera. The viewer's native stop (controller.stop_acquisition then controller.clear_acquisition) is the @estop; the package is R1 because the bound cap.device.configure.v1 class floor is R1, and no estop_physical_ref is claimed (SAFE-045 asks for one only at R2+). NOT COVERED: the image arrays the viewer emits from its Qt callback thread; the standard's image form is an artifact reference and this package has no artifact store, so no image capability (cap.sensing.image.v1) is bound. NOT COVERED: the card's hinted callback_signal (a Qt signal) and roi_pos_size (the viewer's temporary Qt QRectF selection, not the camera ROI; the driver reads the camera controller's ROI instead). native.py constructs the viewer class headless (no PyMoDAQ dashboard and no Qt callback thread) and was never imported or run; PyMoDAQ and pylablib are not installed here and no camera was attached. The fake's camera list, serial, device information, geometry, exposure and ROI are test data, not a device size. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's helper names PythonObjectDriver; this is a direct Driver because the camera state is exposed through a property, a tuple-valued ROI method and a controller object, which the family grammar cannot express.
